prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: World University Rankings 2024: Top Seven (language en).
Grid: 7 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "University" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Country" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Score" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Overall rank" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "University" · longest unbreakable word 109px · one-line width 277px
  col 2: header "Country" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 111px
  col 3: header "Score › Teaching" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 65px
  col 4: header "Score › Research" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 67px
  col 5: header "Score › Citations" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 65px
  col 6: header "Score › Industry" · longest unbreakable word 60px · one-line width 60px
  col 7: header "Overall rank" · longest unbreakable word 51px · one-line width 86px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare the top seven universities by overall rank, country and four performance scores.","reading":"Readers can find a university or rank, then scan across its row and down the score columns to compare institutions. Wrapped names and countries should remain clearly associated with their scores.","groups":["University and Country identify each institution and provide context.","Teaching, Research, Citations and Industry are parallel numerical measures under the shared Score header; consistent spacing helps comparison.","Overall rank is the summary position for each institution."],"keep_intact":["Individual words in university names and countries","Score values and rank numbers","Individual score-column headings"],"may_wrap":["University names at word boundaries, particularly the longer institute names","Country names between words","Overall rank between its two words, using the two-row header height"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [190, 116, 86, 88, 86, 81, 72] · table 720×420px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 36, 60, 36, 60, 36, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/8 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [224, 82, 86, 88, 86, 81, 72] · table 720×490px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/8 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [190, 82, 96, 98, 96, 85, 72] · table 720×490px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/8 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
